4.4a — Attack: Close-Range Danger

The enemy closes in — and now it has to actually hurt you. Contact damage sounds trivial ("touch = −1") until you remember Update runs 60 times a second. The fix is the cooldown pattern from 3.3a, wearing a new coat.

Predict First ~10 min

Read the attack half of EnemyController.cs:

[SerializeField] private int damage = 1;
private float damageCooldown = 1.0f;
private float lastDamageTime = -1.0f;

private void OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D collision)
{
    if (collision.gameObject.CompareTag("Player"))
    {
        TryDamage();
    }
}

private void OnCollisionStay2D(Collision2D collision)
{
    if (collision.gameObject.CompareTag("Player"))
    {
        TryDamage();
    }
}

private void TryDamage()
{
    if (Time.time > lastDamageTime + damageCooldown)
    {
        if (StatManager.manager != null)
        {
            StatManager.manager.ChangeHealth(-damage);
            lastDamageTime = Time.time;
        }
    }
}

Predict: you get grabbed and cannot escape — you stand inside the enemy for 5 seconds. How many hits total? (Careful — Enter fires once; Stay fires continuously. Which one is doing the work after the first second?) And why does lastDamageTime start at −1.0 instead of 0 — what would the very first frame of a collision do differently?

Socratic

Turret cooldown = fire slower. Enemy cooldown = hurt slower. Same pattern, two meanings. What does a designer express with damageCooldown that they cannot express with damage alone — and what would "cooldown 0.1, damage 1" feel like vs "cooldown 1.0, damage 1"?

Build Lab ~20 min

Step 1 — rebuild TryDamage. Comment out its body and retype it: is the cooldown expired? → does the manager exist? → pay the damage, start the cooldown. The −1.0 seed means "the last hit happened 1 second before the scene began" — the very first touch connects immediately, no free grace period. Change it to 0 and walk into the enemy on the first frame: feel the one-second immunity you just invented. Restore −1.

Step 2 — Enter vs Stay. Both handlers call TryDamage — with the cooldown, only the first tick of each second matters. Comment out OnCollisionStay2D's body: you take ONE hit per bump instead of one per second of contact. Now comment out OnCollisionEnter2D instead: standing on the enemy still drains you at 1/second. Which handler is load-bearing for a chase enemy — and which for a floor trap? Argue it.

Step 3 — connect the whole animal. Trace a full encounter out loud, with the fields: spawn → patrol (direction ±1) → you enter 5 units → chase (normalized pursuit) → contact → TryDamage (cooldown gate) → you flee past 5 → the chase if stops matching → patrol resumes. Every sentence is a field or a comparison. If you can narrate it, you own it — and tomorrow (4.5a) you will draw it.

Bug Hunt: The unfair grapple

  1. Set damage to 3 with health 3. What is the entire encounter now — and why is "one-hit kill" a DESIGN statement, not a bug?
  2. Make TryDamage ignore the cooldown (always true). Stand in the enemy for 3 seconds at 60fps. How many hits did you take — and what happened to the death loop from 2.2a?
  3. Change the tag check to "Player2". Why is silence the symptom again — and how long does it take you to find a silent tag bug NOW?
  4. The enemy damages you; you cannot damage it. What single system from 2.1a would you borrow to give the player a counterattack — and why will Unit 8's boss need exactly that?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Attack design

  1. Knockback: should the enemy push you away on contact? What physics component would you nudge — and why does the turret need nothing similar?
  2. Design a damage TIER: enemy near a turret deals 2, lone enemy deals 1. Where must the difference live so each prefab instance can differ?
  3. Commit + push: "4.4a: contact damage + cooldown".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Rebuild TryDamage and explain the −1.0 seed
  • Explain Enter vs Stay and which behavior needs which
  • Narrate a full encounter as fields and comparisons
  • Explain cooldown as a fairness tool, not a nerf
